data_points.quote: A field's recovery factor is the share of the oil originally in place that will ever be produced. Everything beyond that is tertiary or 'enhanced' recovery, and it is where the arithmetic gets interesting: on a field with 3.6 billion barrels in place, like Vedanta's Mangala in Rajasthan, each additional percentage point of recovery is 36 million barrels — more than a year of the field's output.
